title: Yangqin
extract: The yangqin is a trapezoidal Chinese hammered dulcimer, likely derived from the Iranian santur or the European dulcimer. It used to be written with the characters 洋琴, but the first character was changed in the early 20th century to 揚, meaning "acclaimed". It is also spelled yang ch'in. Hammered dulcimers of various types are now very popular not only in China, but also Eastern Europe, the Middle East, India, Iran and Pakistan. These instruments are also sometimes known by the names "santoor" and "cimbalom" and also had an influence on the Khim (ขิม), a Thai classical instrument.
